raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the Muse Spark MoE pooler (8192 → 4096) and unpooler (4096 → 8192) are `ReplicatedLinear`, so at TP8 every rank reads both full BF16 weights on every step: 134 MB per layer, about 8.3 GB per forward over the 62 layers. This PR makes both projections `ColumnParallelLinear` and all-gathers their output columns over TP. Each output column is still computed from the full reduction on one rank; the gather only moves data. Each rank holds `1 / TP` of the weights, which frees 6.8 GiB per GPU for the KV cache.

## Claims

- **Recipe default (TP8 + EP8 + DSpark), 8×MI355X, random 8k in / 1k out:** output throughput is +2.6% to +4.6% at every concurrency (c4: +20%, mostly from the acceptance length), mean TPOT is −1.7% to −9.3%, and mean TTFT is −0.6% to −8.2%.
- **Memory:** model weights 82.36 → 75.58 GiB per GPU, KV cache +4.8% (6,271,180 → 6,573,865 tokens).
- **Trade-off:** a lone short prompt on an idle server is about 4 ms slower (2k tokens: 104.2 → 108.2 ms); 8k and longer are 1–2% faster. See Details.
- **Accuracy:** GSM8K unchanged (paired exact McNemar p = 0.86). Outputs are not bit-identical, because the GEMM summation order changes.
- **Default on** when every TP rank sees the same tokens (TP > 1, no sequence-parallel MoE, DP = 1, not `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`), with the same config switches as the CUDA path. To turn it off: `--hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"muse_spark_tep_shard_pooler": false, "muse_spark_tep_shard_unpooler": false}}'`.
- No change to core files: everything is in `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/`, plus the two new tests in the Buildkite yaml.

## Validation

**Setup.** 8×MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (vLLM `83c078d955`, AITER 0.1.26, torch 2.13, ROCm 10; Python code replaced by the tree under test), `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4` with the `Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark` drafter (7 speculative tokens). The serve command is the AMD Day 0 recipe default: TP8 + `--enable-expert-parallel`, `VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16`, `--max-num-seqs 64`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, CUDA graphs `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, prefix caching off. The baseline is `main` (`83c078d955`) without this PR, on the same machine with the same arguments. Commands are in the collapsed block below.

**Serving**, base → this PR, mean of two runs per concurrency:

| Config | Input / output tokens | Conc | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Verify step (ms) | Accept len |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 + EP8 + DSpark | 8192 / 1024 (random) | 1 | 176.4 → 184.4 (+4.5%) | 278 → 276 (−0.6%) | 5.40 → 5.17 (−4.4%) | 14.69 → 14.07 (**−4.2%**) | 2.72 → 2.73 |
| TP8 + EP8 + DSpark | 8192 / 1024 (random) | 4 | 490.3 → 589.6 (+20.3%) | 514 → 472 (−8.2%) | 6.60 → 5.98 (−9.3%) | 19.20 → 18.95 (−1.3%) | 2.92 → 3.17 |
| TP8 + EP8 + DSpark | 8192 / 1024 (random) | 16 | 1172.9 → 1226.8 (+4.6%) | 938 → 916 (−2.3%) | 11.75 → 11.16 (−5.0%) | 32.28 → 31.98 (−0.9%) | 2.75 → 2.87 |
| TP8 + EP8 + DSpark | 8192 / 1024 (random) | 32 | 1472.0 → 1537.4 (+4.4%) | 1537 → 1514 (−1.5%) | 17.85 → 17.29 (−3.2%) | 49.35 → 48.04 (**−2.7%**) | 2.76 → 2.78 |
| TP8 + EP8 + DSpark | 8192 / 1024 (random) | 64 | 1850.9 → 1898.8 (+2.6%) | 2742 → 2702 (−1.5%) | 29.50 → 29.01 (−1.7%) | 80.09 → 80.64 (+0.7%) | 2.71 → 2.78 |

- On random prompts the acceptance length moves from run to run, so decode is compared by the verify step (TPOT × accept len), the time per target forward. It is −4.2% at c1 and −1% to −3% at c4–c32, where the saved weight reads matter most. At c64 the verify batch is large enough that they are amortized.
- The c4 throughput gain comes mostly from a higher acceptance length; the baseline's second c4 run is also low (416 tok/s, see the per-run values).

**Single request and memory:**

| Config | Input / output tokens | Concurrent requests | TTFT (ms), median |
|---|---|---:|---|
| TP8 + EP8 + DSpark | 2048 / 1 | 1 | 104.2 → 108.2 (+3.8%) |
| TP8 + EP8 + DSpark | 8192 / 1 | 1 | 264.2 → 260.0 (−1.6%) |
| TP8 + EP8 + DSpark | 16384 / 1 | 1 | 538.7 → 531.6 (−1.3%) |
| TP8 + EP8 + DSpark | 8192 / 1 | 4 (burst) | 1036.0 → 1021.2 (−1.4%) |

Model weights 82.36 → 75.58 GiB per GPU; KV cache 6,271,180 → 6,573,865 tokens (+4.8%).

<details>
<summary>Serve and benchmark commands, per-run values</summary>

Serve command (AMD Day 0 recipe):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN_SHORT_QUERY_3D=1 \
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 --served-model-name musespark \
  --tokenizer-mode hf --config-format auto --load-format safetensors --generation-config vllm \
  --language-model-only --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --reasoning-parser musespark1x --tool-call-parser musespark1x --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}'
```

Serving sweep: one warm-up (`--random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 8 --seed 7`), then two runs per concurrency `C`, `R` = 1, 2, averaged:

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --model musespark \
  --tokenizer amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.0 \
  --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $((4 * C > 16 ? 4 * C : 16)) --max-concurrency $C --seed $((1000 * R + C)) \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

Single-request TTFT: K concurrent `/v1/completions` requests with fresh random token-id prompts of L tokens, `max_tokens=1`, `temperature=0`. We take the wall time until all K finish and report the median over n bursts (the first burst is dropped). The cases are (K, L, n) = (1, 2048, 12), (1, 8192, 16), (1, 16384, 8) and (4, 8192, 6).

Per-run serving values:

| C | run | out tok/s base -> PR | mean TTFT ms | mean TPOT ms | AL base / PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 177.1 -> 192.0 | 274 -> 276 | 5.38 -> 4.94 | 2.73 / 2.86 |
| 1 | 2 | 175.7 -> 176.8 | 281 -> 276 | 5.42 -> 5.39 | 2.71 / 2.60 |
| 4 | 1 | 564.7 -> 621.1 | 484 -> 483 | 6.36 -> 5.83 | 3.09 / 3.30 |
| 4 | 2 | 415.9 -> 558.2 | 543 -> 460 | 6.84 -> 6.14 | 2.74 / 3.04 |
| 16 | 1 | 1132.4 -> 1190.0 | 915 -> 909 | 12.05 -> 11.32 | 2.65 / 2.79 |
| 16 | 2 | 1213.5 -> 1263.6 | 961 -> 924 | 11.45 -> 11.01 | 2.85 / 2.94 |
| 32 | 1 | 1497.8 -> 1583.1 | 1551 -> 1499 | 17.93 -> 17.06 | 2.73 / 2.83 |
| 32 | 2 | 1446.3 -> 1491.6 | 1523 -> 1530 | 17.77 -> 17.51 | 2.80 / 2.73 |
| 64 | 1 | 1873.5 -> 1877.5 | 2733 -> 2685 | 29.54 -> 29.19 | 2.72 / 2.76 |
| 64 | 2 | 1828.2 -> 1920.1 | 2752 -> 2718 | 29.46 -> 28.83 | 2.71 / 2.80 |

</details>

**Accuracy**

- GSM8K 5-shot (`lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, 1319 questions, 32 concurrent requests), TP8 + EP8 + DSpark: strict 0.9492 -> 0.9477, flexible 0.9484 -> 0.9469. Paired on strict: 16 questions are correct only on the baseline and 14 only with this PR, exact McNemar p = 0.86.
- Greedy outputs on 5 fixed prompts (45 to 8192 tokens) are not bit-identical: the first-token logprob differs by 0.03–0.34 and 3 of 5 completions diverge. The pooled activations differ by up to 1 BF16 ulp because the GEMM summation order changes, and the experts' MXFP4 activation quantization can turn 1 ulp into a different quantization step.

**Tests and checks** on `main` (`83c078d955`, 8×MI355X, AITER 0.1.26):

- The new tests and the existing Muse ROCm tests (`test_muse_spark_rocm_bf16_moe.py`, `test_muse_spark_moe_finalize.py`, `test_muse_spark_router.py`, `test_muse_spark_rocm_rmsnorm_expand.py`, `test_muse_spark_norms.py`, `tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py`, `test_muse_spark_logits_local.py`): 111 passed.
  - `tests/kernels/test_muse_spark_rocm_skinny_gemm.py`: every output is within one BF16 ulp of an fp64 reference; a cancellation case that any BF16 partial sum would get wrong; determinism, strided input and HIP graph replay.
  - `tests/distributed/test_muse_spark_rocm_shard_pooler.py` (TP2 and TP8, AITER and RCCL gathers, 1 to 8192 tokens, eager and graph): the gathered output is bit-identical to the per-rank blocks, and matches the replicated `F.linear`.
- CI: the two new files are added to the "Distributed" and "Kernels" test areas. The GPU tests need gfx950 with AITER and skip elsewhere.

## Details

**How.**

- `MuseSpark1xMoE` builds the pooler and unpooler with `ColumnParallelLinear` when sharding is on, so each rank loads its `[N / TP, K]` block of the checkpoint weight. `_gathered_column_proj` runs the projection and all-gathers the output columns.
- **All-gather.** AITER's custom all-gather (`dim=-1`, no transpose) when available. Prefill outputs larger than its IPC buffer are gathered in token chunks, which is faster than RCCL (single layer at TP8, 2048 tokens: 128 µs vs 248 µs for the two gathers). Otherwise `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather`.
- **Decode GEMM.** After sharding, N is only 512 (pooler) or 1024 (unpooler), too narrow for hipBLASLt to fill the GPU at decode sizes. Up to 128 tokens on gfx950, `ops/skinny_gemm.py` runs a two-pass split-K Triton GEMM: each split accumulates in fp32, and a second kernel adds the splits in a fixed order in fp32 and rounds to BF16 once. No partial sum is rounded to BF16, so the error is that of an fp32-accumulating GEMM such as `F.linear`. AITER's tuned GEMMs are not used here because their split-K accumulates the partials in BF16. Single MI355X, graph replay: pooler shard 17.4 µs (full `F.linear`) → 4.9 µs at 1 token, unpooler shard 16.0 → 4.8 µs.

**Trade-off: a lone short prompt on an idle server is about 4–11 ms slower.**

- Below about 2.5k tokens, an eager single-request prefill of this model is bound by host-side kernel launches: baseline TTFT stops falling (about 95–100 ms at both 512 and 1024 tokens) while the GPU work keeps shrinking. The two extra all-gathers per layer add about 49 µs of host launch time per layer (about 3 ms per forward) and two cross-rank synchronization points.
- The GPU time of the sharded segment is lower at every prefill size from 256 tokens up (11 to 92 µs per layer), so prefills of 3k tokens and more are faster, and under concurrent traffic prefill chunks are batched with decodes and are GPU-bound.
- The full weights no longer exist on each rank, so a token-count threshold cannot fall back to the replicated GEMMs. Keeping the full weights and sharding only at decode sizes (as the CUDA path does) would avoid this cost but give up the 6.8 GiB per GPU. Users who care most about idle short-prompt TTFT can turn the feature off with the `hf-overrides` above.

**Complexity.** The PR adds 294 non-test lines: `model.py` (+127/−16: the sharded projections, the all-gather and the switches) and `ops/skinny_gemm.py` (167: the split-K kernel and its per-shape configs).

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.

- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

Up to 128 tokens on gfx950, `ops/skinny_gemm.py` runs a two-pass split-K Triton GEMM: each split accumulates in fp32, and a second kernel adds the splits in a fixed order in fp32 and rounds to BF16 once. No partial sum is rounded to BF16, so the error is that of an fp32-accumulating GEMM such as `F.linear`. AITER's tuned GEMMs are not used here because their split-K accumulates the partials in BF16. Single MI355X, graph replay: pooler shard 17.4 µs (full `F.linear`) → 4.9 µs at 1 token, unpooler shard 16.0 → 4.8 µs.

**Trade-off: a lone short prompt on an idle server is about 4–11 ms slower.**

- Below about 2.5k tokens, an eager single-request prefill of this model is bound by host-side kernel launches: baseline TTFT stops falling (about 95–100 ms at both 512 and 1024 tokens) while the GPU work keeps shrinking. The two extra all-gathers per layer add about 49 µs of host launch time per layer (about 3 ms per forward) and two cross-rank synchronization points.
- The GPU time of the sharded segment is lower at every prefill size from 256 tokens up (11 to 92 µs per layer), so prefills of 3k tokens and more are faster, and under concurrent traffic prefill chunks are batched with decodes and are GPU-bound.
- The full weights no longer exist on each rank, so a token-count threshold cannot fall back to the replicated GEMMs. Keeping the full weights and sharding only at decode sizes (as the CUDA path does) would avoid this cost but give up the 6.8 GiB per GPU. Users who care most about idle short-prompt TTFT can turn the feature off with the `hf-overrides` above.

**Complexity.** The PR adds 294 non-test lines: `model.py` (+127/−16: the sharded projections, the all-gather and the switches) and `ops/skinny_gemm.py` (167: the split-K kernel and its per-shape configs).

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Column-sharded MuseSpark1x pooler/unpooler on ROCm: every TP rank projects
+its block of output columns and the blocks are all-gathered, which must give
+the replicated projection's output."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import ray
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm._aiter_ops import is_aiter_found, rocm_aiter_ops
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_tp_group, graph_capture
+from vllm.envs import disable_envs_cache
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+from ..utils import (
+    ensure_model_parallel_initialized,
+    init_test_distributed_environment,
+    multi_gpu_test,
+    multi_process_parallel,
+)
+
+pytestmark = [
+    pytest.mark.skipif(
+        not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="ROCm-only MuseSpark1x model path"
+    ),
+    pytest.mark.skipif(not is_aiter_found(), reason="AITER is not installed"),
+]
+
+HIDDEN, POOLED = 8192, 4096
+# At TP8, up to 128 tokens take the split-K GEMM, and 8192 tokens gather the
+# unpooler output in chunks that fit AITER's buffer.
+NUM_TOKENS = [1, 5, 64, 128, 129, 1000, 8192]
+
+
+def _check_sharded_matches_replicated(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+    tp_size: int,
+    pp_size: int,
+    rank: int,
+    distributed_init_port: str,
+    use_aiter: bool,
+) -> None:
+    with monkeypatch.context() as m:
+        m.delenv("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", raising=False)
+        m.delenv("HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES", raising=False)
+        m.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER", "1" if use_aiter else "0")
+        m.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR", "1" if use_aiter else "0")
+        disable_envs_cache()
+        rocm_aiter_ops.refresh_env_variables()
+
+        from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.model import (
+            MuseSparkShardedProjMethod,
+            _gathered_column_proj,
+        )
+
+        device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}")
+        torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+        init_test_distributed_environment(tp_size, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port)
+        ensure_model_parallel_initialized(tp_size, pp_size)
+        assert (rocm_aiter_ops.get_aiter_allreduce() is not None) == use_aiter
+
+        method = MuseSparkShardedProjMethod()
+
+        def project(weight: torch.Tensor, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+            return method.apply(SimpleNamespace(weight=weight), x)
+
+        gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0)
+        for n, k in ((POOLED, HIDDEN), (HIDDEN, POOLED)):
+            weight = torch.randn(n, k, device=device, generator=gen) * k**-0.5
+            blocks = [b.contiguous() for b in weight.bfloat16().chunk(tp_size)]
+
+            def layer(x: torch.Tensor, w: torch.Tensor = blocks[rank]):
+                return project(w, x), None
+
+            for num_tokens in NUM_TOKENS:
+                x = torch.randn(num_tokens, k, device=device, generator=gen)
+                x = x.bfloat16()
+                out = _gathered_column_proj(layer, x)
+                # The gather only moves bits: each block is what its rank's
+                # GEMM produced, recomputed here from the same weights.
+                local = torch.cat([project(b, x) for b in blocks], dim=1)
+                assert torch.equal(out, local), (n, k, num_tokens)
+                # Both GEMMs accumulate in fp32 and differ only in summation
+                # order, so outputs differ by at most an ulp, and rarely.
+                replicated = F.linear(x, torch.cat(blocks))
+                mismatch = (out != replicated).float().mean().item()
+                assert mismatch < 5e-2, (n, k, num_tokens, mismatch)
+                torch.testing.assert_close(out, replicated, atol=2e-2, rtol=1e-2)
+
+            # Decode steps replay CUDA graphs.
+            x = torch.randn(4, k, device=device, generator=gen).bfloat16()
+            expected = _gathered_column_proj(layer, x)
+            with graph_capture(device=device) as ctx:
+                graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+                with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=ctx.stream):
+                    out = _gathered_column_proj(layer, x)
+            graph.replay()
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+            assert torch.equal(out, expected)
+        get_tp_group().barrier()
+
+
+@ray.remote(num_gpus=1, max_calls=1)
+def gather_with_aiter(monkeypatch, tp_size, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port):
+    _check_sharded_matches_replicated(
+        monkeypatch, tp_size, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port, use_aiter=True
+    )
+
+
+@ray.remote(num_gpus=1, max_calls=1)
+def gather_with_rccl(monkeypatch, tp_size, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port):
+    _check_sharded_matches_replicated(
+        monkeypatch, tp_size, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port, use_aiter=False
+    )
+
+
+@multi_gpu_test(num_gpus=2)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("test_target", [gather_with_aiter, gather_with_rccl])
+def test_column_sharded_projection_tp2(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, test_target):
+    multi_process_parallel(monkeypatch, 2, 1, test_target)
+
+
+@multi_gpu_test(num_gpus=8)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("test_target", [gather_with_aiter, gather_with_rccl])
+def test_column_sharded_projection_tp8(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, test_target):
+    multi_process_parallel(monkeypatch, 8, 1, test_target)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""fp32-accumulating split-K GEMM for the TP-sharded MuseSpark1x projections."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.ops.skinny_gemm import (
+    _CONFIGS,
+    skinny_gemm,
+    skinny_gemm_config,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="requires a ROCm GPU"
+)
+
+# Pooler and unpooler column shards at TP8.
+SHAPES = [(512, 8192), (1024, 4096)]
+
+
+def _bf16_ulp(t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """One BF16 unit in the last place at each element of ``t``."""
+    exponent = torch.frexp(t.float())[1]
+    return torch.ldexp(torch.ones_like(t, dtype=torch.float32), exponent - 8)
+
+
+def test_config_lookup():
+    for (n, k), rows in _CONFIGS.items():
+        for max_tokens, *_ in rows:
+            assert skinny_gemm_config(n, k, max_tokens) is not None
+        assert skinny_gemm_config(n, k, rows[-1][0] + 1) is None
+        for max_tokens, _, block_n, block_k, splits, _ in rows:
+            assert n % block_n == 0 and k % (splits * block_k) == 0
+    assert skinny_gemm_config(4096, 8192, 1) is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n,k", SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 2, 7, 8, 16, 33, 64, 100, 128])
+def test_skinny_gemm_rounds_the_fp32_sum_once(n, k, num_tokens):
+    """Each output is the fp32 sum rounded to BF16 once, like an fp32-accumulating
+    ``F.linear``: within one BF16 ulp (plus the fp32 summation error) of an fp64
+    reference, and almost always equal to that reference rounded to BF16."""
+    torch.manual_seed(num_tokens * n)
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    w = (torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda") * 0.02).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+    out = skinny_gemm(x, w)
+    ref = x.double() @ w.double().t()
+    assert out.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and out.shape == (num_tokens, n)
+
+    # fp32 summation error, far below what one BF16-rounded partial would add.
+    fp32_err = 2**-20 * (x.double().abs() @ w.double().abs().t())
+    bound = _bf16_ulp(ref).double() + fp32_err
+    linear = F.linear(x, w)
+    for y in (out, linear):
+        assert ((y.double() - ref).abs() <= bound).all()
+        assert (y != ref.bfloat16()).float().mean().item() < 1e-2
+    # Same inputs, same order of the fixed split reduction.
+    assert torch.equal(out, skinny_gemm(x, w))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n,k", SHAPES)
+def test_skinny_gemm_does_not_round_partials_to_bf16(n, k):
+    """Large partial sums that cancel: a partial rounded to BF16 (8 significant
+    bits) would drop the remainder of 12 that fp32 keeps exactly."""
+    x = torch.ones(4, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    w = torch.empty(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    half = k // 2
+    w[:, :half] = 1024.0
+    w[:, half:] = -1024.0
+    w[:, 0] = 1032.0
+    w[:, -1] = -1020.0
+    out = skinny_gemm(x, w)
+    assert torch.equal(out, torch.full_like(out, 12.0))
+
+
+def test_skinny_gemm_strided_rows_and_empty():
+    n, k = 1024, 4096
+    w = torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    base = torch.randn(16, 2 * k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    x = base[:, :k]
+    assert not x.is_contiguous() and x.stride(1) == 1
+    assert torch.equal(skinny_gemm(x, w), skinny_gemm(x.contiguous(), w))
+    assert skinny_gemm(x[:0], w).shape == (0, n)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n,k", SHAPES)
+def test_skinny_gemm_replays_in_a_graph(n, k):
+    x = torch.randn(8, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    w = torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    expected = skinny_gemm(x, w)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        out = skinny_gemm(x, w)
+    x.copy_(torch.randn_like(x))
+    expected = skinny_gemm(x, w)
+    graph.replay()
+    assert torch.equal(out, expected)

+def _chunked_aiter_all_gather_columns(ca, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+    """AITER's column all-gather of ``x`` in token chunks that fit its IPC
+    buffer; prefill-sized gathers are faster this way than through RCCL."""
+    row_bytes = x.shape[1] * x.element_size()
+    rows = ca.max_size // (ca.world_size * 2) // row_bytes
+    # AITER needs every chunk, including the last partial one, 16-byte aligned.
+    if row_bytes % 16 or not 0 < rows < x.shape[0] or not ca.should_custom_ag(x[:rows]):
+        return None
+    out = x.new_empty(x.shape[0], x.shape[1] * ca.world_size)
+    for start in range(0, x.shape[0], rows):
+        end = min(start + rows, x.shape[0])
+        ca.all_gather_unreg(x[start:end], out=out[start:end], dim=-1)

+    out, _ = layer(x)
+    return _all_gather_columns(out)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Split-K BF16 GEMM for few-token activations against a narrow weight.
+
+``y = x @ w.T`` with ``x`` ``[M, K]`` (M small) and ``w`` ``[N, K]``. Each split
+accumulates its K range in fp32; a second kernel adds the splits in fixed order,
+in fp32, and rounds to BF16 once. No partial sum is ever rounded to BF16, so the
+error matches an fp32-accumulating GEMM such as ``F.linear`` (the results differ
+from it only through the summation order), and the output is deterministic for
+a given M.
+
+A single-kernel "last split reduces" variant is slower on MI355X: the
+agent-scope acquire/release it needs flushes and invalidates the per-XCD L2.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+# (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K, splits, num_warps)
+_Config = tuple[int, int, int, int, int]
+
+# (N, K) -> ((max tokens, *_Config), ...), tuned on MI355X with the weight
+# streamed from HBM and the calls replayed from a HIP graph.
+_CONFIGS: dict[tuple[int, int], tuple[tuple[int, int, int, int, int, int], ...]] = {
+    # Muse Spark pooler, column-sharded over TP8.
+    (512, 8192): (
+        (16, 16, 16, 256, 16, 4),
+        (32, 32, 16, 256, 16, 2),
+        (64, 32, 16, 256, 8, 4),
+        (128, 16, 64, 256, 8, 4),
+    ),
+    # Muse Spark unpooler, column-sharded over TP8.
+    (1024, 4096): (
+        (8, 16, 16, 256, 8, 2),
+        (16, 16, 16, 256, 8, 4),
+        (32, 32, 16, 256, 8, 2),
+        (64, 32, 16, 256, 4, 4),
+        (128, 64, 64, 256, 8, 4),
+    ),
+}
+
+
+def skinny_gemm_config(n: int, k: int, num_tokens: int) -> _Config | None:
+    """The tuned config for ``[num_tokens, k] @ [n, k].T``, or None."""
+    for max_tokens, *cfg in _CONFIGS.get((n, k), ()):
+        if num_tokens <= max_tokens:
+            return tuple(cfg)  # type: ignore[return-value]
+    return None
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _skinny_gemm_kernel(
+    x_ptr,
+    w_ptr,
+    y_ptr,
+    part_ptr,
+    M,
+    stride_xm,
+    stride_ym,
+    N: tl.constexpr,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    SPLITS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pid_n = tl.program_id(0)
+    pid_k = tl.program_id(1)
+    pid_m = tl.program_id(2)
+    K_PER_SPLIT: tl.constexpr = K // SPLITS
+    offs_m = pid_m * BLOCK_M + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
+    offs_n = pid_n * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
+    m_mask = offs_m < M
+    acc = tl.zeros([BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N], dtype=tl.float32)
+    for kk in range(0, K_PER_SPLIT, BLOCK_K):
+        offs_k = pid_k * K_PER_SPLIT + kk + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
+        a = tl.load(
+            x_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * stride_xm + offs_k[None, :],
+            mask=m_mask[:, None],
+            other=0.0,
+        )
+        b = tl.load(w_ptr + offs_n[None, :] * K + offs_k[:, None])
+        acc = tl.dot(a, b, acc)
+    if SPLITS == 1:
+        tl.store(
+            y_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * stride_ym + offs_n[None, :],
+            acc.to(y_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+            mask=m_mask[:, None],
+        )
+    else:
+        tl.store(
+            part_ptr + (pid_k * M + offs_m[:, None]) * N + offs_n[None, :],
+            acc,
+            mask=m_mask[:, None],
+        )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _reduce_splits_kernel(
+    part_ptr,
+    y_ptr,
+    M,
+    stride_ym,
+    N: tl.constexpr,
+    SPLITS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    offs = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offs < M * N
+    acc = tl.load(part_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    for s in tl.static_range(1, SPLITS):
+        acc += tl.load(part_ptr + s * M * N + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    tl.store(
+        y_ptr + (offs // N) * stride_ym + offs % N,
+        acc.to(y_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+        mask=mask,
+    )
+
+
+def skinny_gemm(
+    x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, config: _Config | None = None
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``x @ weight.T`` for 2-D bf16 ``x`` and a contiguous ``[N, K]`` weight.
+
+    ``config`` defaults to the tuned entry, which must exist for this shape.
+    """
+    assert x.dim() == 2 and x.stride(1) == 1 and weight.is_contiguous()
+    m, k = x.shape
+    n = weight.shape[0]
+    assert weight.shape[1] == k
+    out = torch.empty((m, n), dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+    if m == 0:
+        return out
+    if config is None:
+        config = skinny_gemm_config(n, k, m)
+        assert config is not None, f"no skinny GEMM config for {(m, n, k)}"
+    block_m, block_n, block_k, splits, num_warps = config
+    # The kernel loads the weight unmasked.
+    assert n % block_n == 0 and k % (splits * block_k) == 0
+    part = (
+        torch.empty((splits, m, n), dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+        if splits > 1
+        else out
+    )
+    _skinny_gemm_kernel[(n // block_n, splits, triton.cdiv(m, block_m))](
+        x,
+        weight,
+        out,
+        part,
+        m,
+        x.stride(0),
+        out.stride(0),
+        N=n,
+        K=k,
+        SPLITS=splits,
+        BLOCK_M=block_m,
+        BLOCK_N=block_n,
+        BLOCK_K=block_k,
+        num_warps=num_warps,
+    )
+    if splits > 1:
+        block = 1024
+        _reduce_splits_kernel[(triton.cdiv(m * n, block),)](
+            part, out, m, out.stride(0), N=n, SPLITS=splits, BLOCK=block, num_warps=4
+        )
+    return out
